LESSON: SILENT READING

Grade: Grade 2
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: READING
Topic 3.3: Silent reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Silent reading
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: When do we read learner should be able to: silent reading skills for efficient silently?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. read texts and passages silently reading(through guiding questions, 3 lessons
2. read silently showing sustained timing reading) focus for longer periods (15-20  Learners discuss questions after silent minutes) reading in pairs and groups
3. answer comprehension questions  Learner should be provided with from texts read follow-up activities for sustained silent

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Silent reading

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Silent reading

Teach
• Focus skill: read texts and passages silently reading(through guiding questions, 3 lessons.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Silent reading.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Silent reading
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. When do we read learner should be able to: silent reading skills for efficient silently?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
